gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the cheapest new Synology target, the DS124 at $159.99 on Amazon today, costs less than every non-Synology NAS on the shortlist (UGREEN DH2300 $239.99, TerraMaster F2-425 $269.99, UGREEN DXP2800 $389.99), even though Synology's spec says those rsync-type targets can't take Hyper Backup's entire-system backups. It also doesn't state that the DS124 costs the same as about 23 TB-months of Backblaze B2 at $6.95 per TB a month.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited: Synology's Hyper Backup tech spec (www.synology.com/en-ro/dsm/7.4/software_spec/hyper_backup), which lists destinations by backup type but no models or prices, and the KB 'Destination' help page, which only showed navigation when I opened it. The uncited B&H compare, Newegg and Adorama pages blocked my fetch (HTTP 403). ChatGPT's answer prices only the DS124 ($159.99, B&H) and DS223j ($214.99, Adorama). It never prices a non-Synology NAS against them, and it never compares a box against a per-TB cloud price. Its 'used DS118/DS120j $50–100' and 'Pi $50–100' figures are, in its own words, 'target ranges, not verified live listings'.
decides: This confirms the DS124 as the cheapest new pick and removes the reason to send buyers to a third-party NAS. Each non-Synology box listed here costs more today, and Synology's spec limits rsync servers to folder and package backup. Our own UGREEN DH2300 and DXP2800 rows should be framed as 'only if you also want a general home NAS', not as cheaper backup targets. For a small data set (about 1–2 TB), B2 at $6.95/TB/month undercuts the DS124 box for roughly 1–2 years before you even buy a drive.

findings.note: Break-even against the DS124 box alone: 159.99 / 6.95 ≈ 23 TB-months. That is about 23 months for 1 TB, 11.5 months for 2 TB, 5.8 months for 4 TB. Drive cost excluded, so the real break-even is later.

findings.label: Hyper Backup destinations by backup type
findings.value: Entire system: remote Synology NAS and Synology C2 only. Folder/package: adds rsync servers, S3-compatible and others. Up to 65,535 versions. AES-256 client-side encryption. Destination needs at least 8 GB free.
